scope: Park consensus groups while their queued/in-flight log write awaits an exact sync receipt. No physical latency or capacity qualification in this slice.
implementation: Derive persistence waiting from the existing Ready/light/apply/checkpoint/snapshot-abort phases; do not add another mutable durability flag. Uninstalled snapshots remain eligible for physical install/abort work.
Remove persistence waiters from the runnable queue without removing their independent FIFO write slots, reservations, deferred requests, coalesced ticks or hints.
Exact validated sync receipts wake their groups; rejected candidates wake failure reports. Backend admission overload preserves FIFO ordering and the existing retry deadline.
Existing acknowledgement, Ready, image-publication and resource-limit rules are unchanged. Global completion errors retain their fail-closed behavior.

reproducer.observed: 32 groups awaiting new-term persistence remain in the runnable queue on the original scheduler. The focused regression fails at that bound.
reproducer.fixed: Hold the real persistence future, serve 32 unrelated heartbeats, then verify that each batch releases only its matching response set after actual engine persistence.
reproducer.selection_correction: The initial command combined a short filter with --exact and selected zero tests; it is retained and is not validation. The corrected selector executes one test and reproduces the intended failure.

regressions: queued/in-flight waits leave runnable queue while independent heartbeat service continues
deferred per-group admission remains bounded and charged; coalesced hints/ticks survive
pre-I/O injected overload preserves FIFO and retry backoff
real engine candidate rejection reports failure and permits the next batch
mismatched receipt group identities never wake or acknowledge waiters
notes: The overload test injects a backend refusal before polling the I/O future; it supplies no success receipt. The candidate rejection test exercises the real engine with a term-regressing queued candidate.

Final unit inventory and all 96 unit cases were rerun after making the new backoff assertion independent of a ten-millisecond wall-clock race. Production sources were unchanged during integration validation.
These tests establish scheduler behavior and durability boundaries, not the cause of every prior physical queue/latency burst.

findings: The prior 1,500-cell control throughput drops during the same observation intervals as queue buildup and longer sample/SQL phase durations; correlation does not identify the causal sub-operation.
The prior repeated 150-cell control ends with host load averages 22.93/15.93/11.79 and 12,517 MiB swap used on a 32-GiB Mac. Its first control meets traffic targets.

Current Colima inventory has default (2 GiB) and cellar-raft-perf (16 GiB) running; the dedicated five-node profile (22 GiB) is stopped. Configured VM limits would total 40 GiB, which is not a measure of actual resident memory.

limitations: No new physical benchmark was launched; the dedicated profile remains stopped and other profiles were not mutated. Original physical outcomes and source pins are unchanged.
This removes demonstrated redundant scheduler work during persistence waits. Its contribution to the earlier shared-host latency and control-queue bursts is not established.
No equivalent-contract speedup, sustained S3 latency, Q1 capacity, independent failure domains, Amazon S3 or soak qualification.
